title: How the Orthodox Church Can Reach Americans
description: Recorded 2025 The Catechist Certification Program—offered by St. Vladimir’s Online School of Theology with the blessings of His Beatitude Metropolitan Tikhon and His Eminence Metropolitan Saba—was launched in response to the recent waves of inquirers, seekers, and catechumens at Orthodox churches across North America. It is not a catechesis but a training program for aspiring catechists. These professionals help support their priests or even work full-time in parish life, promoting Church growth in this moment that our merciful Lord is entrusting to us. The program drew nearly 130 participants for its most recent cohort, who are completing their training this July. The next cohort will be formed in September. title: Church Etiquette for Families
description: Walking into an Orthodox church with young children can feel overwhelming—but it doesn’t have to be. In today’s video with Patristic Nectar Family, we’re sharing practical church etiquette for families: how to prepare before Liturgy, entering and exiting the Church, when to step out, how to help children participate, and simple ways to cultivate reverence without expecting perfection. Children don’t learn to love the Church by staying home until they’re “old enough.” They learn by being there—week after week, surrounded by prayer, worship, and the life of the Church. Whether you’re new to Orthodoxy, visiting for the first time, or have been bringing little ones to church for years, I hope this conversation encourages you. 🎥 Watch the full episode now, and let me know in the comments: What’s one church etiquette tip that has helped your family? Be sure to download the Patristic Nectar App to listen to the daily synaxarion for the lives of the saints! Its free! Find us on Instagram: @PatristicNectarFamily If you want to see more PN Family's Content, please consider making a donation! title: Traveling as an Orthodox Christian
description: Traveling as an Orthodox Christian? ✈️☦️ In this video, I’m sharing a few simple ways to stay connected to the life of the Church while traveling, including: • How to find a canonical Orthodox parish wherever you go • Helpful etiquette when visiting another parish • A few things I always bring with me when I travel • Why you shouldn’t skip coffee hour! One of the greatest blessings of Orthodoxy is that wherever we travel, we can worship together and be welcomed as family. To find a canonical Orthodox parish near your destination, visit the Assembly of Bishops parish directory: https://www.assemblyofbishops.org/directories/parishes/ Have you ever attended an Orthodox church while traveling? Share your favorite experience below! ☦️ Be sure to download the Patristic Nectar App to listen to the daily synaxarion for the lives of the saints! Find us on Instagram: @Asceticlifeofmotherhood and @PatristicNectarFamily If you want to see more PN Family's Content, please consider making a donation! title: 5 Miracles That Happen at Baptism

title: Christian Marriage
description: Welcome back to Heavenward! Grab a mug and join Pres Catherine and her daughters as we talk about the beautiful role of women in a Christian marriage. Links & episode info: Enduring Love Book: https://www.amazon.com/Enduring-Love-Christian-Foundations-Marriage/dp/1735011657 Prayer for One’s Spouse “Oh Lord Jesus Christ our God, our Sweet Savior, who taught us always to pray for each other, so that by thus fulfilling the holy law, we will be made worthy of Thy mercy: look down with compassion on our married life, and keep from all perilous falls, from enemies visible and invisible, my husband whom Thou hast granted me, that we may pass our time together until the end with oneness of mind. Grant him health, strength, and fullness of wisdom enlightened from above, so that he may be able to fulfill his duties all the days of this life, according to Thy will and commandments. Protect and keep him from temptations, and may he be able to bear and conquer those temptations that come upon him. Strengthen him in right faith, strong hope, and perfect love, so that together we may do good deeds and that we may order all our life according to thy divine ordinances and commandments. Amen..” Whether you are a daughter, mother, sister, godmother, auntie, or grandmother, Heavenward offers meaningful conversation, encouragement, and a Christ-centered perspective. Subscribe to Patristic Nectar Family for more Orthodox Christian podcasts, discussions, and family-focused content. Be sure to download the Patristic Nectar App and find us on Instagram: @PatristicNectarFamily If you want to see more PN Family's Content, please consider making a donation! title: I No Longer Live - Sunday after Exaltation 2023
description: The Arena Podcast is the flagship of Patristic Nectar Publications and contains the Sunday Sermons and other theological reflections by Father Josiah Trenham delivered from the ambon of St. Andrew Church in Riverside, California, and begun in 2010. Currently, there are more than 600 sermons and lectures covering ten years worth of preaching through the liturgical calendar. | Links | 2023 PNP Conference Registration Open Now "Every Thought Captive: Cultivating the Christian Mind" All-access live-stream, in-person, recorded lectures for $40 Guest Speakers: Fr Alexis Torrance and Pres. Dr. Jeannie Constantinou www.conference.patristicnectar.org (http://www.conference.patristicnectar.org) Demonology: Understanding & Winning the Spiritual Battle Access Lectures Here (https://patristicnectar.org/bookstore_220620_11222221112) PNP is pleased to present a new six-lecture series by Father Josiah Trenham entitled Demonology: Understanding and Winning the Spiritual Battle. The study of the Church’s demonology is a part of basic catechism and Christian instruction. The Scriptures are replete with teachings about the dark powers. Additionally, it is impossible to appreciate the magnitude of the saving deeds of our Savior, the Lord Jesus Christ, without understanding how He, and He alone, has conquered Satan and destroyed his works. Lastly, Christians are called to fight and win in the spiritual war, and for this reason, it is essential that believers understand their enemies and their tactics. Toward this end, Father Josiah presents in these lectures in-depth studies of the Scriptures, Divine Services, and pedagogy of great saints and teachers on the subject of Satan and spiritual battle. Lecture titles include: Lecture #1 Jesus and Satan Lecture #2 Demonology in the Baptismal Rite and the Divine Liturgy Lecture #3 Gaining Mastery of Satan: The Life of St. Anthony the Great Lecture #4 How to Win the Spiritual Battle according to St. John of the Ladder Lecture #5 Engaging the Unseen Warfare: Fr. Lorenzo Scupoli and St. Nicodemos of the Holy Mountain Lecture #6 C. S. title: Abraham Our Father
description: The Arena Podcast is the flagship of Patristic Nectar Publications and contains the Sunday Sermons and other theological reflections by Father Josiah Trenham delivered from the ambon of St. Andrew Church in Riverside, California and begun in 2010. Currently there are more than 550 sermons and lectures covering ten years worth of preaching through the liturgical calendar. | Links | Sirach: Fashioning a Life of Wisdom | 5 Lectures https://patristicnectar.org/bookstore_220620_112 Patristic Nectar Publications is pleased to present a new five-lecture series by Father Josiah Trenham entitled Sirach: Fashioning a Life of Wisdom. The Wisdom of Sirach or Ecclesiasticus, as the book is known in the Western or Latin tradition, is a choice composition from the Wisdom literature of the Old Testament. Written in the 2nd century BC in Hebrew and translated into Greek by the author's grandson in Alexandria, Egypt, this majestic portion of Holy Scripture combines the rich aphorisms of traditional Hebrew sapiential literature with the concerns and background of 2nd-century Hellenic culture. Jesus, the Son of Sirach, was highly prized by the Church Fathers from the earliest days of the Church. In these five lectures, Father Josiah hones in on the themes of learning and seeking wisdom, humility, work, wealth, almsgiving, friendship, social life, wives, women, medicine and physicians, youth and aging, and wise speech and the power of words. In this video, Father will take your little ones on a spiritual journey, simplifying the Sunday gospel readings so that kids can better understand the Sunday Liturgy. 🙏 What to Expect: A warm and friendly introduction by Father Joseph. A simplified explanation of the Sunday gospel reading, making it relatable and engaging for kids. Thought-provoking questions to spark discussion and reflection. Inspiring messages to encourage your children's faith and love for Jesus. This video is perfect for children of all ages, whether they're new to the faith or have grown up in the Orthodox tradition. It's a wonderful way to introduce them to the beauty of the gospel and its teachings. title: Heavenward: Hospitality and Meals on a Budget
description: In this episode of Heavenward, we talk about how to prepare nourishing meals for your family without overspending. From simple planning tips to budget-friendly ingredients, we share practical ways to feed your household well while keeping costs down. Thoughtful cooking, wise stewardship, and a little creativity can go a long way in the kitchen. Recipe from Pres Catherine: - Tomato, basil, garlic, Kalamata olive and. shrimp over linguine (or rice, or barley) - *2-3 cups fresh minced basil *8 cloves of garlics pressed *1 onion chopped *5 tomatoes chopped *1/2 cup olive oil *1/2 cup fresh grated Parmesan cheese (for topping) 16 oz jar of Kalamata olives chopped 1 lb whole shrimp (cleaned, washed and drained) *cooked linguini , rice or barley Sautee onion and garlic in olive oil, when soft, add tomatoes and stir for 3 mins, add basil, olives simmer and stir for another 3 mins Scoop linguini and add warm sauce on top and top with fresh Parmesan - Salsa verde Chicken Tacos - *whole cooked chicken (pull all meat off the bone and put in a pot) *add 1 whole jar (or two) of salsa verde (or even better…make your own) *1 -2 cups of northern beans (add to chicken mixture) *cut up for toppings: -5 green onions -1 bunch of cilantro chopped -chopped olives -2 chopped tomatoes -1 whole chopped jalapeño -shredded jack cheese Recipe from Victoria: - Cookies - 4 cups almond flour 1/2 cup butter or coconut oil 1 tsp baking soda 1-2 tsp vanilla extract 1/2 tsp salt 2-3 scoops Protein powder (optional, but we use paleo valley a chocolate bone broth protein) Adding 1/4 cup peanut butter is an option as well Add chocolate chips Bake at 350 for 9 minutes Recipe from Stasi: - Recipe for Thai curry - • 1 cup basmati rice • 1 pound medium shrimp (or chicken) • Salt and pepper to taste • 2 tablespoons coconut oil or butter • 1 onion, diced • 1 red bell pepper, diced (or whatever veggies you have on hand — sometimes we use potatoes) • 2 tablespoons red curry paste • 3 cloves garlic, minced • 1 tablespoon freshly grated ginger • 1 (13.5-ounce) can coconut milk • 3 cups vegetable stock or bone broth • 2 tablespoons freshly squeezed lime juice • 2 tablespoons chopped fresh cilantro leaves • • Season shrimp (or chicken) with salt and pepper, to taste. • Melt butter in a large stockpot or Dutch oven over medium high heat. Add shrimp (or chicken) and cook, stirring occasionally, until pink, about 2-3 minutes; set aside. • • Add onion and bell pepper to the Dutch oven. Cook, stirring occasionally, until tender, about 3-4 minutes. • Stir in red curry paste, garlic and ginger until fragrant, about 2 minutes. • Stir in coconut milk and vegetable broth (or bone broth) ; season with salt and pepper, to taste. Bring to a boil; reduce heat and simmer until slightly thickened, about 8-10 minutes. • Stir in rice, shrimp, lime juice and cilantro • Coconut rice: 2 cups rice, 1 15 oz can coconut milk, 1.5 cups water and dash of salt (and maybe a little maple syrup) bring to boil and cover let simmer for 20 mins

title: The Kind of Fasting God Rejects
description: As we approach Great Lent, Father Josiah Trenham reflects on what it truly means to fast in a way that pleases God. Drawing from the Gospel parable of the Publican and the Pharisee and the teaching of the Prophet Isaiah, this talk explains why fasting without humility and repentance is empty, and how true fasting deepens prayer, heals the heart, and renews our spiritual life. 00:00 Preparing for Great Lent 02:05 The Fast That Condemns Instead of Heals 04:33 Fasting Without Repentance Is Empty 05:00 Isaiah 58 and God’s Rebuke 08:36 What True Fasting Looks Like Download the *Patristic Nectar App* everywhere! title: Heavenward: God Has Sent the Perfect People for You
description: Heavenward: A Women’s Podcast is a new offering from Patristic Nectar Family rooted in Orthodox Christian faith and values. In this episode, Presbytera Catherine is again joined by her adult daughters, Victoria and Anastasia, for an intergenerational conversation on faith, womanhood, family, and the Christian life. Together, they share Orthodox Christian wisdom, lived experience, and thoughtful reflections for women of all ages. Whether you are a daughter, mother, sister, godmother, auntie, or grandmother, Heavenward offers meaningful conversation, encouragement, and Christ-centered perspective. title: Blasphemy Laws
description: In this reflection, Father Josiah Trenham explores whether blasphemy laws are truly un-American. Drawing from Christian history, early American legal tradition, and constitutional reasoning, he argues that reverence for God’s name was once understood as foundational to civic peace and moral order. title: Don’t Torment Your Guardian Angel
description: As Christmas approaches, Father Josiah reflects on the ancient Christian teaching of the guardian angel and how one is given to each believer at holy baptism. Drawing from Holy Scripture, the Psalms, and the writings of St. Basil the Great and St. Macarius, he explains how sin does not only grieve God, but also torments our guardian angel. 0:00 – Preparing for Christmas and the angelic realm 0:18 – Guardian angels given at baptism 1:12 – Christ’s teaching on guardian angels (Matthew 18) 1:35 – Psalm 33 and angelic protection 1:49 – St. Basil on driving away your angel by sin 2:26 – One angel as an entire encampment 3:06 – How Christians should relate to their guardian angel 3:30 – Story of St. Macarius and the weeping angel 5:28 – “He has become a slave of the demons” 5:36 – A warning about sins of the flesh 6:00 – Prayers for a guardian of soul and body 6:25 – Angels and the Nativity of Christ 7:05 – Final exhortation Download the *Patristic Nectar App* everywhere! title: 🍁 St Martin's Day Lantern Procession ⭐️
description: The lantern procession tradition on St. Martin's Day, celebrated on November 12, is a cherished tradition honoring St. Martin of Tours (397 AD). In Germany, children make lanterns and parade through the streets, singing songs. The lanterns shining in the dark are often interpreted as symbolizing the light of Christ, a particularly appropriate image for the beginning of the Nativity Fast (November 15th). St Martin is a beloved Saint celebrated throughout the world and is known for his merciful compassion on the needy. St. Martin's Day is celebrated on November 12th in the Eastern Orthodox Church. To learn more about St Martins day, check out my blogpost at: https://www.asceticlifeofmotherhood.com/blog/martindayprocession St Martin book: Snow on Martinmas https://www.amazon.com/dp/B06WGPJGG4?ref=cm_sw_r_ffobk_cso_cp_mwn_dp_BP054EZZ3K903GGHGW18&ref_=cm_sw_r_ffobk_cso_cp_mwn_dp_BP054EZZ3K903GGHGW18&social_share=cm_sw_r_ffobk_cso_cp_mwn_dp_BP054EZZ3K903GGHGW18&bestFormat=true Be sure to download the Patristic Nectar App to listen to the daily synaxarion for the lives of the saints! title: Our Favorite Orthodox Family Habit - and Why We Love the PNP App!
description: Let's explore this simple daily habit (and some easy ways to incorporate it into your home) of reading the lives of the saints to our children. Let's explore why we should create this habit and answering some FAQs such as "are my kids too young?" Further more! When we gather as a family to read the lives of the saints, we’re doing something far more than simply telling stories. Reading the saints daily keeps our faith alive in the home. It reminds us that holiness isn’t something distant or impossible — it’s what we’re ALL called to. And when our children grow up hearing these stories day after day, they begin to see the world differently. They learn that suffering is a participation in Christs suffers, that love is stronger than fear, and that every ordinary moment can be filled with Christ. This daily habit becomes like the lighting of a small lamp — one that keeps burning in the heart of your family. Through the witness of the saints, our homes are filled with the sweet smelling fragrance of faith, and our children come to know that they too are called to be part of this great story — the story of Christ lived out in His saints. Be sure to download the Patristic Nectar App to listen to the daily synaxarion for the lives of the saints! title: Rotten Priests
description: In this reflection, Father Josiah draws from Scripture and Church tradition to speak candidly about the reality of rotten priests. title: How Orthodox Christians Pray and Eat at the Table - with Ascetic Life of Motherhood
description: Eating as a family with small children takes intention, patience, persistence, and tender love and care. Although I grew up eating as a family, it’s becoming less and less common. As a mother with 4 small children, I can understand why. It’s hard work! But the seeds that are planted in their hearts through your patience and persistence will bear good fruit. My oldest is only 9 and I am already seeing the fruit of our labors. Here are some tips we have picked up along the way: ~ Assign jobs for both setting the table and clearing the table - I have found that keeping these same jobs for 1-2 months helps build confidence and allows the children to take ownership of them. All I have to say now is “Do you job” and they already know what to do! It makes meal times much smoother. ~ Sing and pray before each meal! This is the glue for every meal and a way of inviting christ into our homes. We are asking for God’s blessing while also expressing our gratitude! ~ Wait for everyone to be done eating, and ask to be excused - Being polite is always good, and instilling these manners is ideal at meal times. ~ Everyone brings their plate to the counter to be washed - This helps everyone! We are both being responsible for our own messes, but we are also assisting in the work. This can be done as early as 18 months old! I start my kids very young in sharing the load. They find so much satisfaction in this work! What would you add to the list? title: St Euphrosynos the Cook Saint - baked apples recipe with Ascetic Life of Motherhood
description: St Euphrosynos feast day is September 11th! You can find this September monthly printable at www.asceticlifeofmotherhood.com/store/septhrudec Baked Apples of Paradise for the feast of St Euphrosynos! 3 TBSP unsalted butter, softened 1/4 C packed brown sugar 1/2 tsp cinnamon 1/8 tsp nutmeg 1/4 C old-fashioned rolled oats 3 large apples 1. Preheat oven to 375°F 2. Mash the butter, sugar, cinnamon, and nutmeg together until combined. Stir in the oats. 3. Core the apple with a sharp knife of apple corer about 3/4 down and scoop out a little and be sure the seeds are removed. 4. Place cored apples in a pie dish. Spoon filling into each apple, filling all the way to the top. Pour warm water into the dish around the apples. Bake for 40-45 minutes or until apples appear slightly soft. Serve warm with ice cream!

title: Bishop Irenei on Sacraments Outside the Church
description: In this teaching, Bishop Irenei addresses the often-asked question: Does the Orthodox Church acknowledge sacraments outside her life? He explains that the Orthodox understanding of the sacraments (or mysteries) is rooted in the life of the Church as the Body of Christ. title: Day in the Life of our Orthodox Homeschool with Ascetic Life of Motherhood
description: ☦️ Welcome to our little corner of Orthodox homeschooling—where our days begin with prayer, unfold at a slow and thoughtful pace, and follow the life-giving rhythms of the Church. Here, we celebrate feast days with joy, read aloud from living books, and seek to surround ourselves with all that is good, beautiful, and true. Our family life is about connection—working together, praying together, and growing together in Christ. Every lesson, every story, every rhythm of our day is about building a strong foundation in Him, so that when our children go out into the world, they go rooted in their true identity: their life in Christ. You can find more resources on my blog about how we follow the Liturgical cycle in our home at Asceticlifeofmotherhood.com My children are 9, 6, 4 and 2, so here are our curriculum choices this year: - Bible: Children’s Bible Reader -Children’s Synaxarion: Potamitis Publishing (My Synaxarion: August) - Christian education - @asceticlifeofmotherhood (still in the works to complete for sharing) - Nature Study (Science) - @treehouse_schoolhouse - Geography/Cultural Studied - Beautiful Feet Around the World Part 1 - Math - @thegoodandthebeautiful - Language Arts - @thegoodandthebeautiful - Reading - Teach your child to read in 100 easy lessons - Art - St Raphael Schole (Online) - Introduction to Iconography - History - state history co op taught by a dear friend

title: The Revolutionary Manifesto of Jesus
description: In this reflection, Fr. title: Does the Church Curse Those Outside the Church?
description: Bishop Irenei explains the true meaning of "anathema" in the Orthodox Church. Far from being a curse, the anathemas proclaimed on the Sunday of Orthodoxy are pastoral warnings, pointing out the boundaries of the Christian faith and lifting souls to God’s mercy. title: What 10 Years of Same-Sex Marriage Has Meant for America

title: St Herman of Alaska Cookies
description: St. Herman’s Rustic Honey Cookies Recipe (Simple, nourishing, humble) Ingredients 1 cup whole grain flour (rye or barley was more common than wheat) 1/4 cup oats 2–3 tbsp honey 2 tbsp coconut oil (traditionally would have been seal or bear oil) Pinch of salt Small handful of dried berries (like cranberries or blueberries), if available Water to bind (2–4 tbsp) Instructions Preheat oven to 350°F Mix flour, oats, salt, and dried berries. Add honey and coconut oil, mixing with a spoon or fingers. Add a little water at a time until a dough forms. Shape into small, flat discs. Bake 350°F for 15–20 min until bottom is golden brown. Enjoy warm! ⚪️ Icon used in video: Uncut Mountain Supply ⚪️ Children’s Book: 101 Orthodox Saints by Ancient Faith Publishing ⚪️ Sacred Alaska Film: sacredalaskafilm.com ⚪️ Wooden Icon: https://sthermanstudios.com/ ⚪️ St Innocent Orphanage (Project Mexico) https://www.projectmexico.org

title: Do Heretical Churches Have Apostolic Succession?

title: Blessing of Grapes for Holy Transfiguration
description: On August 6th, we celebrate the glorious Feast of the Transfiguration of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. This is one of the 12 Great Feasts in the Orthodox Church. In the Orthodox Church, it is customary to bring grapes and other first fruits to church on this day to be blessed and distributed to the faithful. Why grapes? Grapes were traditionally among the earliest fruits of the summer harvest. Offering them to God is a way of giving thanks for His provision—of saying, “We receive all good things from You, and we return them with gratitude.” But grapes carry even deeper spiritual meaning for us. Grapes, when pressed, become wine. And wine, offered on the altar, becomes the Blood of Christ. So these humble fruits become a powerful symbol—not just of thanksgiving, but of transformation. Just as grapes are changed, we too are called to be changed—to be transfigured, to become partakers in the divine life. After the blessing, we take these grapes home—and there are so many simple and meaningful ways to use them. 🟣 Share them: Offer a small plate to a friend or neighbor. Just like the loaves and fishes, the blessed fruits of the Church are meant to be shared. 🟣 Make a simple lenten-friendly charcuterie board with fruits, olives, nuts, and bread. Since the feast falls during the Dormition Fast, it’s a beautiful way to honor the day while keeping the fast. 🟣 Include children: Let little ones help wash the grapes, arrange them, and light a candle as you read the Gospel story of the Transfiguration together. 🟣 Feast with joy: This is a fast day, but the Church gives us a joyful exception: we’re allowed wine, oil, and even fish on this feast. It’s a day of light and gladness, and the Church invites us to celebrate. Blessed feast! Please, Like and Subscribe to our channel at Patristic Nectar Kids! description: Father Joseph Thornburg Welcome to our special YouTube Kids edition of Father Jason's Sunday Gospel Homily! Discover how Elias's life foreshadows the Incarnation, the miracles of Christ, and the coming of the Holy Spirit. title: Living Liturgically: Following the Orthodox Church Calendar
description: 😅 Feeling overwhelmed by the Church calendar? You’re not alone. Liturgical living can feel like trying to drink from a firehose 🚿—especially when you’re new to Orthodoxy. But what if we slowed down and embraced it one step at a time? 🕊️✨ In this video, I’m sharing how we’ve begun weaving the rhythm of the Church into our home life—and how you can too, without burnout or guilt. Here’s a peek at one of our new family traditions: 🎉 A simple, meaningful feast day meal for St. Marina—complete with “🔥 Super Fast Dragon Noodles” (yes, really!) 🍜🐉 As we ate, we read her life and talked about how she crushed the devil (aka the dragon) with the power of the Cross. 🩸✝️🛡️ Scroll down for the recipe + some encouragement on sustainable liturgical living. Let’s bring the Church home, one beautiful day at a time. 🏡🕯️ Super Fast Dragon Noodles for the feast of St Marina 1 Package of Squiggly Knife cut noodles from Trader Joes 1 Package of stir fry vegetables 1 Tbsp olive oil 1 Tbsp brown sugar 1 garlic clove (crushed) or 1 tsp garlic powder 1 tsp crushed ginger or 1 tsp ginger powder Top of sesame seeds or green onions Cook noodles according to package directions. In a bowl, mix the provided sauce packets, along with 1 TBSP brown sugar, 1 crushed garlic clove, and 1 tsp ginger. Mix well. Saute vegetables in 1 tbsp oil, until soft and slightly browned. Add cooked noodles to the sautéed vegetables and add sauce to the top. With low heat, mix the vegetables, noodles, and sauce until well incorporated. Serve immediately and add sesame seeds and green onions to garnish. This recipe came together in 10 mins, and as we ate, we read the life of St Marina, and discussed how she overcame the temptations of the devil (traditionally portrayed as a dragon) and defeated him with the cross. Please, Like and Subscribe to our channel at Patristic Nectar Kids! description: Celebrate the feast of St. Joanna, one of the Myrrhbearing Women, with this easy homemade playdough craft! 👐✨ As you mix and knead, talk with your kids about the sweet smell of holiness and the beautiful gifts the Myrrhbearers brought to Christ’s tomb. 🕊️💐 📝 Ingredients: 🥣 1 cup flour 🧂 1/4 cup salt 🍋 1 tbsp cream of tartar 🌻 1 tbsp vegetable oil 🔥 3/4 cup boiling water 🌈 Natural food coloring (optional) 🌸 A few drops of essential oils (lavender, frankincense, rose, etc.) 👩‍🍳 Instructions: 1️⃣ Mix dry ingredients in a bowl 2️⃣ Add oil + boiling water 3️⃣ Stir until combined, then knead 4️⃣ Add essential oils + knead again 💡 Perfect for little hands and big conversations about faith 🕯️💖 #StJoanna #MyrrhbearingWomen #OrthodoxKids #FaithAndCrafts #PlaydoughRecipe #LiturgicalLiving #OrthodoxMoms #HomemadePlaydough #SweetSmellOfHoliness

title: The Double Gaze
description: This Pentecost reflection, titled The Double Gaze, explores the profound moment of Christ's Ascension—how Jesus, while blessing the disciples, fixed his loving gaze on them as He rose to the right hand of God. Discover how this gaze continues today, through the ministry of the Holy Spirit, and how Christians return that gaze by setting their hearts on things above. title: The Feast of Pentecost
description: Father Jason Covarrubias 🙏 What to Expect: A warm and friendly introduction by Father Jason. A simplified explanation of the Sunday gospel reading, making it relatable and engaging for kids. Thought-provoking questions to spark discussion and reflection. title: Sunday of the Blind Man
description: Father Joseph Thornburg Join us for a joyful and simple homily for children on the Sunday of the Blind Man! In this Gospel story, Jesus heals a man born blind—and shows us how He brings light to our hearts too. Kids will learn how to see with faith, trust Jesus, and understand His love through this powerful miracle. Perfect for Orthodox families and Sunday school! Welcome to our special YouTube Kids edition of Father Jason's Sunday Gospel Homily! In this video, Father Jason will take your little ones on a spiritual journey, simplifying the Sunday gospel readings so that kids can better understand the Sunday Liturgy. 🙏 What to Expect: A warm and friendly introduction by Father Joseph. A simplified explanation of the Sunday gospel reading, making it relatable and engaging for kids. Thought-provoking questions to spark discussion and reflection. Inspiring messages to encourage your children's faith and love for Jesus. This video is perfect for children of all ages, whether they're new to the faith or have grown up in the Orthodox tradition. It's a wonderful way to introduce them to the beauty of the gospel and its teachings. title: Ending Atheistic Education
description: In this reflection, Father Josiah Trenham responds to a recent Supreme Court ruling involving a Catholic charter school in Oklahoma. He uses the case to highlight deeper concerns about the lack of school choice, the forced public funding of anti-Christian education, and the overall decline of moral and academic standards in the U.S. education system. Why are families restricted from directing their tax dollars to schools that reflect their values? What are the long-term effects of an aggressively secular public school system? Is there hope for restoring freedom and faith in American education? title: Painting Water Jars for the Sunday of the Samaritan Woman
description: Christ is risen! This Sunday we commemorate the Samaritan woman, or the Women at the Well, known to us as St Photini. To remember this beautiful encounter, we’re going to do a simple and meaningful craft. We’ll paint flowers on a glass water jar—a symbol of the living water Jesus spoke about. ☦️🫙💧🌺 Here’s what you’ll need: A clean glass jar, pitcher, or holy water jar Acrylic paint or paint pens Paint brushes Mod podge Choose Light, joyful colors—blues, whites, pinks, even gold. You can paint flowers, vines, or even drops of water - symbols of life! You can paint directly onto the jar. As you paint, think about what “living water” means to you. What has Jesus healed or renewed in your own life? After your painting is dry, you can paint a layer of mod podge over it to make it waterproof. This jar or pitcher will be a reminder in your home of the transformed life of St Photini and the living waters that Christ offers each of us. If you paint a jar, tag Patristic Nectar Kids so we can share your beautiful creations! To learn more, check out our video with Fr Jason on the Samaritan Woman (https://youtu.be/W5NogJXs3Gk?feature=shared) Find us on Instagram: @Asceticlifeofmotherhood and @PatristicNectarKids If you want to see more PNP Kids Content, please consider making a donation! title: The Heresy That Denied Repentance
description: Father Alexis Torrance & Father Josiah Trenham What happens when Christians believe repentance is impossible after serious sin? In this compelling conversation, Fr. Josiah Trenham and Fr. Alexis Torrance explore the early Church heresy of Novatianism and its rejection of mercy for apostates. Learn why the Church condemned this puritanical movement, and discover the deep meaning of Christlike repentance—repenting not just for ourselves, but for others. title: Artist's Corner | Saint Mary of Egypt
description: Join us at our Artist's Corner for guided art projects with stories of great saints! Listen to the life of St Mary of Egypt and draw a lion with our artist in today's video. April 1st is the Nameday of St Mary of Egypt. The Wednesday before the Fifth Sunday of Lent is marked by special prayers and hymns that highlight Saint Mary of Egypt's repentance and ascetic struggles. This midweek observance helps believers reflect on her steadfast commitment to God and prepares them to fully engage with her commemoration on Sunday. Saint Mary’s life teaches that transformation is possible through humility and reliance on God. Her commemoration during Lent inspires Orthodox Christians to complete their spiritual journey with hope and courage as they approach the celebration of Pascha, the Resurrection of Christ! Saint Mary and Saint Zosimas remind us to trust in God’s forgiveness and strive for holiness. May their story inspire us to live with faith and humility. #orthodoxchristianity #patristicnectar #patristicnectarpublications #patristicnectarkids #easternorthodoxy #lent #biblestoriesforkids #biblestoriesforchildren #stmaryofegypt #drawwithme #artforkids #christianchildrencontent #chrisitanity

title: Planting a Mary Garden - Celebrating the Annunciation with Ascetic Life of Motherhood
description: 🌷 In Medieval times, it became popular to create “Mary Gardens”, gardens full of flowers and herbs that were named after the Mother of God. For the feast of the Annunciation, in honor of the day that the Theotokos (Mary) said yes to God, we planted the start of our own Mary Garden, using seeds of flowers that are named for her. 🌷 There are over 1,100 flowers that honor Mary. Here are a few that you may be familiar with, with their medieval names: • Amaryllis – “Beautiful lady” • Baby’s breath – “Lady’s veil” • Bachelor’s buttons – “Mary’s crown” • Bleeding heart – “Mary’s heart” • Buttercup – “Lady’s locks” • Carnation – “Mary’s love of God” • Chamomile – “Lady’s flower” • Columbine – “Our Lady’s shoes” • Dandelion – “Mary’s bitter sorrow” • Fern – “Lady’s hair” • Forget-me-not – “Eyes of Mary” • Foxglove – “Our Lady’s gloves” • Geranium – “Lady beautiful” • Honeysuckle – “Lady’s stick” • Impatiens – “Our Lady’s earrings” • Iris – “Mary as Queen” • Larkspur – “Mary’s tears” • Lily-of-the-valley – “Our Lady’s tears” • Marigold – “Mary’s gold” • Morning glory – “Our Lady’s mantle” • Ox-Eye daisy – “Mary’s star” • Pansy – “Our Lady’s delight” • Petunia – “Lady’s praise” • Rose – a symbol of Mary herself (she is known as the “Mystical Rose”) • Rosemary – “Mary’s nosegay” • Sweet pea – “Our Lady’s flower” • Tulip – “Mary’s prayer” • Violet – “Our Lady’s modesty” • Zinnia – “Little Mary” Find us on Instagram: @Asceticlifeofmotherhood and @PatristicNectarKids For more information on my blog to plant your own Mary garden: www.asceticlifeofmotherhood.com/blog/marygarden-2025 If you want to see more PNP Kids Content, please consider making a donation! title: Jesus Heals the Paralyzed Man (Kids Homily)
description: Father Joseph Thornburg Welcome to our special YouTube Kids edition of Father Jason's Sunday Gospel Homily! In this video, Father Jason will take your little ones on a spiritual journey, simplifying the Sunday gospel readings so that kids can better understand the Sunday Liturgy. 🙏 What to Expect: A warm and friendly introduction by Father Joseph. A simplified explanation of the Sunday gospel reading, making it relatable and engaging for kids. Thought-provoking questions to spark discussion and reflection. title: Lent: Tips for Orthodox Families
description: Have you ever wanted to learn more about Lent and the different ways you can cultivate your own Lenten journey with your own family? Great Lent is a special gift that the Church gives us in order to help us re-focus our lives on Christ. The Church has set aside 40 days as a special time of repentance and calls us to a long and sustained spiritual effort. It is comparable to a school of repentance in which every Christian can go yearly in order to deepen their faith, re-evaluate, and, if possible, to change their lives. It’s a wonderful journey to the very source of the Orthodox faith; a rediscovery of the Christian way of life. As we recognize this significant shift in our liturgical calendar, I wanted to provide resources and ideas to help you cultivate a lenten environment in your homes and with your families and share our favorite breakfast smoothie recipe! Berry Smoothie Makes 1 smoothie! Handful of spinach 1/2 banana 2 tbsp peanut butter 1 tbsp chia seeds 1 tbsp hemp hearts 1 tbsp flaxseed 3/4 cup frozen berries 3/4 cup water (or coconut water) Blend and serve immediately. title: Monastery Soup for the Feast of St Anthony the Great | PNP Kids
description: Monastery Soup for the Feast of St. Anthony the Great On January 17th, we celebrate St. Anthony the Great! Honor his feast day with this simple, hearty monastery-style soup, perfect for a cozy dinner paired with candlelight and crusty bread. Lighting a candle transforms an ordinary meal into a special celebration! While enjoying your meal, listen to the Life of St. Anthony on the Patristic Nectar App (find it under the synaxarion for the day). Afterward, spark a meaningful family discussion about what stood out in his inspiring life. Recipe: 3 tablespoons oil of choice 1 cup barley 1 carrot, finely grated 2 leeks, sliced 1 bay leaf 1/3 cup fresh parsley, minced Salt to taste 7 cups water or vegetable broth Directions: Heat the oil in a soup pot and toast the barley, stirring continuously for 1 minute. Add the carrot, leeks, bay leaf, parsley, salt, and 7 cups of water. Cook over low to medium heat, covered, for 40–45 minutes, until the barley is tender. Add more water if needed. For extra flavor, add bouillon and mushrooms during the last 20 minutes of cooking. Remove the bay leaf and serve hot. Additional Resources: Listen to Life of St. Anthony on Patristic Nectar App: Patristic Nectar Synaxarion: https://app.patristicnectar.org/discover/synaxarion?date=2025-01-17 St. Anthony for Kids Blog Post: Ascetic Life of Motherhood Blog: https://www.asceticlifeofmotherhood.com/blog/stanthonythegreat Icon: Uncut Mountain Supply: https://www.uncutmountainsupply.com/icons/of-saints/by-name/a/st-anthony-the-great-20th-c-1an53/ Book - Life of St. Anthony by St. Athanasius: Amazon: https://www.amazon.com/Life-Anthony-Athanasius/dp/1631740318 Audiobook: Audible: https://www.audible.com/pd/Life-of-St-Anthony-of-Egypt-Audiobook/B07TS9HRK6?source_code=ASSORAP0511160006&share_location=pdp Celebrate the life of St. Anthony with this nourishing meal and a deeper connection to his story!

title: Vasilopita Tradition with Ascetic Life of Motherhood and PNP Kids
description: Let's make Vasilopita with whole wheat flower and honey! If you're unfamiliar with vasilopita, it's a special cake make on New Years to commemorate St Basil's feast day (Jan 1)! This tradition is said to be based on the story that follows: During a time of famine, the emperor demanded an excessive tax from the people of Caesarea, so each family had to give up all their valuables – money and/or jewelry. Upon finding out this injustice, St. Basil fearlessly defended his people, calling the emperor to repentance. The emperor was moved by St. Basil’s speech, canceled the tax and returned all the valuables to the Saint. The Saint was faced with a daunting task: out of a large amount of items, he had to return each one to its rightful owner. He prayed, then prepared a huge cake and baked the treasures inside of it. After calling his flock to prayer, he blessed and cut the cake, offering a piece to each person. Miraculously, each owner received his own valuables in his piece of the cake. Vasilopitas have been baked on St. Basil’s feast day every year since his repose, to commemorate this miracle. Recipe: Vasilopita with whole wheat flour and honey 6 eggs, in room temperature 2 sticks grass fed butter 1 cup honey 1 cup orange juice 2 cups whole wheat flour 1/2 cup almond flour 1.5 tbsp baking powder Zest of two orange Shredded coconut to decorate 1. Preheat your oven at 360F and butter a 10 inches round baking sheet 2. Separate the egg whites from the egg yolks 3. In a mixing bowl beat the egg whites until they form a soft meringue 4. In a separate mixing bowl beat well the egg yolks and butter to incorporate 5. Add the honey and continue to beat until it is well incorporated 6. Add the orange juice and zest and stir 7. Add the whole wheat flour, almond flour and baking powder and stir 8.Stir in *slowly* the meringue in 3 batches using a folding motion 9. Place the cake batter into the baking sheet 10. Bake for at least 45 min and then start checking with a knife or toothpick if it comes out clean. It might take up to 1 hour to bake fully. 11. When ready, let it cool down before you decorate with shredded coconut

this tradition is said to be based on the story that follows: during a time of famine, the emperor demanded an excessive tax from the people of caesarea, so each family had to give up all their valuables – money and/or jewelry. upon finding out this injustice, st. basil fearlessly defended his people, calling the emperor to repentance. the emperor was moved by st. basil’s speech, canceled the tax and returned all the valuables to the saint. the saint was faced with a daunting task: out of a large amount of items, he had to return each one to its rightful owner. he prayed, then prepared a huge cake and baked the treasures inside of it. after calling his flock to prayer, he blessed and cut the cake, offering a piece to each person. miraculously, each owner received his own valuables in his piece of the cake. vasilopitas have been baked on st. basil’s feast day every year since his repose, to commemorate this miracle. recipe: vasilopita with whole wheat flour and honey 6 eggs, in room temperature 2 sticks grass fed butter 1 cup honey 1 cup orange juice 2 cups whole wheat flour 1/2 cup almond flour 1.5 tbsp baking powder zest of two orange shredded coconut to decorate 1. preheat your oven at 360f and butter a 10 inches round baking sheet 2. separate the egg whites from the egg yolks 3. in a mixing bowl beat the egg whites until they form a soft meringue 4. in a separate mixing bowl beat well the egg yolks and butter to incorporate 5. add the honey and continue to beat until it is well incorporated 6. add the orange juice and zest and stir 7. add the whole wheat flour, almond flour and baking powder and stir 8.stir in *slowly* the meringue in 3 batches using a folding motion 9. place the cake batter into the baking sheet 10. bake for at least 45 min and then start checking with a knife or toothpick if it comes out clean. it might take up to 1 hour to bake fully. 11. when ready, let it cool down before you decorate with shredded coconut videos

title: Saint Nicholas, the Gold Coin Tradition, and Resources from Ascetic Life of Motherhood | PNP Kids
description: Celebrate St. Nicholas Day with Patristic Nectar Kids! Welcome to a joyful tradition of the Church! If you’re new to celebrating St. Nicholas Day, I’m thrilled to share this special feast with you. It’s a meaningful and fun way to bring the life of the Church into your home and create lasting family memories. In the Orthodox Church, we honor saints on their feast days, and St. Nicholas' feast day is December 6th. A beloved tradition is leaving out shoes on the evening of December 5th—don’t forget to join in the fun! If you’re new to celebrating feast days as a family, this is the perfect one to start with. title: Koliva | Traditional Memorial Dish with Ascetic Life of Motherhood and PNP Kids
description: 🥣 Koliva recipe 3 cups of uncooked wheat berries (bought mine from Amazon) 2 cups of finely chopped walnuts (or nut of choice) 1 cup golden raisins 1 cup pomegranate seeds 1 cup graham crackers (crushed) 1 tbsp ground cinnamon 1-1/2 cups powdered sugar (for topping) Jordan almonds for decoration Prepare wheat berries according to package directions. Usually have to boil for 40-60 mins and then cool. Once the wheat berries have boiled, drain and rinse and lay on a baking sheet to dry out using paper towels below and above. Once cooled, they will be ready to assemble. Mix all ingredients together, minus the powdered sugar. Put mixed items into a bowl and flatten the berries using your hand or parchment paper. title: We Must LOVE our Enemies
description: Father Jason Covarrubias Welcome to our special YouTube Kids edition of Father Jason's Sunday Gospel Homily! In this video, Father Jason will take your little ones on a spiritual journey, simplifying the Sunday gospel readings so that kids can better understand the Sunday Liturgy. 🙏 What to Expect: A warm and friendly introduction by Father Jason. A simplified explanation of the Sunday gospel reading, making it relatable and engaging for kids. Thought-provoking questions to spark discussion and reflection. title: Akutaq | A Traditional Alaskan Dessert for Saint Peter the Aleut on PNP Kids
description: 🍨 Today for the feast of St Peter the Aleut, we are going to make a traditional Alaskan treat called Akutaq (pronounced a-goo-duck) which is a Yupik word that means “mix them together”. You may have heard it called “Alaskan Ice Cream” as well! This dish has been made with a variety of ingredients that would be plentiful in Alaska including animal fat from whatever animals were hunted like moose, caribou, fish, seal, whales. Then they would add sweet roots, and foraged berries. Mixed together it becomes a healthy tasty treat that would give them lots of strength and healthy nutrients! This would be a dish that St Peter the Aleut would likely have eaten as it was often sent with hunters on their long journey. So today let’s learn how to make this traditional Alaskan dish using just a few simple ingredients! Ingredients: 1 cup lard (or Crisco) 1 cup sugar 2 cups of frozen berries (blueberries, salmon berries, cranberries, etc.) Wooden bowl Take the lard and add it to the bowl. Whip it up with your hand for at least three to five minutes until it’s creamy and fluffy. Pour at least a cup of sugar into the mixture (estimate). And whip it up until the sugar dissolves. Add the frozen berries to the mixture. And mix it up. Add more berries to the mixture if you want more. The akutaq should have a lot of berries in it. Now the akutaq is ready to eat! Will keep in the fridge for a few days!

title: Saint Phanourios | Patron Saint of Lost Things with Ascetic Life of Motherhood & PNP Kids
description: Have you ever heard of St. Phanourios, the patron saint of lost things? St Phanourios is known in the Orthodox Church as a saint who helps people find lost or stolen items. We ask St. Phanourios to help us find whatever we lost, and when we find it, we bake a cake and share it with friends and loved ones to give thanks. This special tradition comes from Greece and the special olive oil citrus cake is called “Phanouropita!” You can also bake this cake on his feast day, August 27th. In this episode, we are baking phanouropita donuts, which is ideal for sharing with others, an important element in the tradition! You can read more about this tradition and find the recipe on my blog: https://www.asceticlifeofmotherhood.com/blog/phanouropita-donuts Ingredients 1-1/4 cups vegetable oil (or substitute for oil of choice) 2-1/2 cups sugar 1-1/4 cups warm water Grated rind of 1 orange 1/2 cup orange juice (fresh orange juice is best) 1/2 tsp cinnamon 3 tsp baking powder 4 cups white flour 1/2 cup chopped walnuts (optional) 1/4 cup raisins (optional) Instructions Preheat your oven to 350 degrees. Sift flour, baking powder, and cinnamon together in a large bowl and set aside. Using a whisk, combine oil and sugar until blended. Add the warm water, orange rind, orange juice, and walnuts and mix well. Slowly add the flour mixture and combine until smooth. Add raisins and walnuts (if adding). Pour batter into well-greased donut pans. Bake at 350 degrees for 20 minutes or until the cake springs back when lightly touched. Cool on a wire rack. Top with powdered sugar.

description: Father Jason Covarrubias Welcome to our special YouTube Kids edition of Father Jason's Sunday Gospel Homily! In this video, Father Jason will take your little ones on a spiritual journey, simplifying the Sunday gospel readings so that kids can better understand the Sunday Liturgy. 🙏 What to Expect: A warm and friendly introduction by Father Jason. A simplified explanation of the Sunday gospel reading, making it relatable and engaging for kids. Thought-provoking questions to spark discussion and reflection. It's a wonderful way to introduce them to the beauty of the gospel and its teachings. title: What is the Dormition Fast? PNP Kids Presents - Ascetic Life of Motherhood
description: In today’s episode we are talking about the Dormition fast and how that might look in your family! Let’s find some ways to pray together, fast, attend the Divine Services and give to those in need. The Dormition Fast is the final fasting season in the Liturgical year. It is one of the four fasting periods of the Orthodox Church year. The duration of the Dormition Fast is always August 1-14th, concluding on the Great Feast of the Dormition of the Theotokos (August 15th). As we recognize this significant shift in our liturgical calendar, I wanted to share some ways to embrace the Dormition Fast in your home! title: How We Celebrate Name Days with Ascetic Life of Motherhood on PNP Kids
description: 🎂 How we celebrate name days in our family. ♥️ A name day is the feast day of your patron saint! Typically we are named after this saint, either at birth or when we join the church, so if you have a patron saint, your name day is the day your patron saint is celebrated! ⛪️ If a service is offered, go to Church on your name day! 🖼️ Display the icon of your saint in a prominent place. 📖 Read the story of their life. 🫖 Host a name day party and invite friends.Focus on service - serve your guests or find a way to serve in the community.Eat your meals on a “God Grant you many years plate”. 🎵 Sing God Grant you many years and say a prayer to your saint! Name day gifts in our house are usually a new Orthodox book. 📸 Take a picture each year with your icon and watch as you grow up with your Saint.How do you celebrate name days in your house?#patristicnectarkids #saints #nameday #feastday #orthodoxkids #orthodoxchurch #orthodoxsaints #happyfeast #sundayschool #homeschool #sahm #christianhome #orthodoxfamily #kidscontent

title: BIG NEWS For Patristic Nectar
description: https://patristicnectar.org In celebration of our 14th year of ministry, we are excited to announce a significant gift to our followers: all of our Theological Lectures are now available completely FREE! This marks a radical shift in our ministry's approach, reflecting our commitment to sharing more content for free and we believe it aligns with God's calling for us. We hope this change brings more people closer to God by having Orthodox Christian online content more accessible and available to anyone without the barrier of fees. This step is a huge leap of faith for us, and we invite you to join us in prayerfully considering how you can support this new chapter. Your monthly donation, no matter the amount, will help sustain and expand our efforts to provide enriching content online. title: Cloud Slime Activity | Feast of the Ascension with PNP Kids
description: Join Ascetic Life of Motherhood in a cloud slime activity! The feast of the Ascension is celebrated 40 days after Pascha, so this year, we celebrate on June 13th! Cloud Slime Ingredients: 1 Cup of cornstarch 1/2 Cup of Inexpensive Conditioner Directions: Combine conditioner and cornstarch in a large mixing bowl and stir until dough forms. Finish kneading by hand until the dough is no longer sticky. We used 1/2 cup of conditioner and 1 cup of cornstarch, but you can make a bigger or smaller batch by adjusting the amounts. All you need to do is stick to a ratio of 2:1 or 2 parts cornstarch and 1 part conditioner. #patristicnectarkids #feastdays #orthodoxchristian #Orthodoxy #orthodoxfamily #christianfamily #christiantradition #kidsactivity #sundayschool #homeschool #familylife #kidscraft #slime

title: Saint Emilia | Plant a Fruit Bearing Tree with Ascetic Life of Motherhood & PNP Kids
description: 🌱 Saint Emilia is a beautiful example of Christian motherhood. One can see the great virtue in her life, primarily through her children—the fruits of her labor and faith. As a mother, I find it inspiring that others are striving to raise Saints and, even more so, those who have succeeded at this monumental task! 🌱 It has been my desire to add fruit-bearing trees to our home each year, so I am using St Emilia as my inspiration, someone whose life produced so much good fruit. As we remember her each year, we can be re-inspired to produce good fruit through the spiritual effort in our lives. Of course, it takes YEARS to produce good fruit. So we must continue to tend to the garden, and when we fail, get up quickly and continue the task at hand. 🌱 As we add more fruit-bearing plants/trees to our property, we reclaim Eden, a glimmer of paradise. I hope to encourage parents to see their vocation as creating for themselves a little church and a slice of paradise in their own homes and in their children's hearts. title: Saints Constantine and Helen | Ascetic Life of Motherhood on PNP Kids
description: On May 21st, for the feast of St. Constantine and Helen, make homemade pesto for dinner with fresh basil! It’s said that St Helen discovered the True Cross of Christ buried under basil (a symbol of victory)! In a food processor or blender, blend up: 2 cups basil leaves ½ cup pine nuts 2 tablespoons fresh lemon juice 1 small garlic clove ¼ teaspoon salt and black pepper to taste ¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for a smoother pesto ¼ cup freshly grated Parmesan cheese Serve over chicken or with pasta! 🖥️Monthly Liturgical Printables from Ascetic Life of Motherhood: https://www.asceticlifeofmotherhood.com/store Grab some cute peg dolls: https://www.etsy.com/listing/1564357827/elevation-of-the-cross-peg-doll-set?ref=share_v4_lx Please remember to donate to Patristic Nectar to help our ministry grow and to see more content from it. title: Lazarakia for Lazarus Saturday | Ascetic Life of Motherhood on PNP Kids
description: Lazarakia for Lazarus Saturday Jesus raised his friend Lazarus from the dead, and we commemorate this miracle and saint tomorrow on Lazarus Saturday. Your family can have a tangible way to participate in this feast by making this traditional bread. 🖥️ Lazarus Saturday Printable from Ascetic Life of Motherhood: https://www.asceticlifeofmotherhood.com/store/lazarusbuns 🍞 Ingredients 6-1/3 cup (800g) of all-purpose flour 1-1/2 cups of lukewarm water 1 packet of yeast 3/4 cup of sugar 1 tsp of cinnamon 1/4 cup of olive oil 1/4 teaspoon of ground cloves (optional) 1/4 cup finely chopped walnuts (optional) 1/4 cup raisins (optional) whole cloves or chocolate chips to decorate the eyes ✍🏽 Instructions Mix the dry ingredients (including yeast) together and knead for 1 minute, then add oil and lukewarm water. Knead well until the batter becomes a nice soft dough. You can now add in nuts or raisins if using. Cover and let the dough rest for about 45 minutes in a warm place. Preheat the oven to 400°F . Line two baking sheets with parchment paper. To shape each of the balls into small men, roll them out into an oblong shape, create a small ball to place as the head and press on top, and form two skinny strips and place them across the body in the shape of an “x” to represent arms. Insert 2 whole cloves or chocolate chips on the head to create the eyes. Should make 15-20 Lazarakia, depending on the size. Place the Lazarakia on the baking sheets. Bake for 20 minutes or until the bread rolls turn golden brown. Cool before serving. 🌹 Icon from @legacyicons https://legacyicons.com/resurrection-of-lazarus-athos-icon-f242/ Dont forget to donate to Patristic Nectar to help our ministry grow and if you want to see more content from our ministry. title: Veneration of the Precious and Life Giving Cross | Lenten Recipe with Ascetic Life of Motherhood.
description: The 3rd week of Great Lent with Ascetic Life of Motherhood! Recipe Crock Pot Lasagna Soup, serves 6 1 medium onion, diced 3 garlic cloves, minced 4 ½ cups vegetable broth ¾ cup dried brown lentils 1 teaspoon dried basil 1 teaspoon dried oregano 2 14 ounce can diced tomatoes 1 tbsp tomato paste 8 lasagna noodles, broken into pieces 3 cups chopped spinach leaves Optional: serve with vegan ricotta cheese (see below) Vegan Ricotta 1 1/2 cups raw cashews, soaked 1/2 cup water juice of 1 large lemon or 1 tablespoon apple cider vinegar 1 – 2 tablespoons nutritional yeast, optional 1 small garlic clove 1/2 teaspoon onion powder Directions: Place the onion, garlic, basil, oregano, lentils, broth, chopped tomatoes, and tomato paste into the slow cooker and stir a few times to blend. (optional: saute onion and garlic prior). Cover with lid and cook on high for 4 hours. 15 mins before serving, add the noodles and spinach to the slow cooker and give the mixture a stir. Allow the soup to continue cooking until noodles are tender and the spinach is wilted, about 15 minutes. Season the soup with salt and pepper to taste. optional top with vegan cashew ricotta (recipe below) Vegan Ricotta Directions: ​​Soak cashews: let cashews sit in hot water for 5 minutes. Blend: Drain cashews and place all remaining ingredients into a blender or food processor, process until creamy stopping to scrape down the sides every few minutes. Taste for flavors adding any additional ingredients.

title: Don't Miss Out! 2024 PNP Conference "The Sacred Arts" | March 29 -31, 2024 | Riverside, California
description: Tickets are only $60 for in-person, live stream, and recordings. Access the Live Stream here: https://crowdcast.io/c/sacredarts/FktJG "The Sacred Arts: Preaching the Gospel Without Words" When: March 29 - 31, 2024 Speakers: Fr. Maximos Constas Jonathan Pageau Lecture 1 - The Origin of Sacred Art Lecture 2 - How Iconography Preaches the Gospel Lecture 3 - How to Read An Icon Lecture 4 - How Architecture Preaches the Gospel Lecture 5 - How Music Preaches the Gospel Sermon by Fr. Maximos Constas Friday Night - Young Adult Mixer with Pub Trivia! Register here: www.conference.patristicnectar.org Where: Riverside, California, or watch live from your screen ———SOCIAL MEDIA——— Patristic Nectar Instagram: https://bit.ly/3kmupqE Patristic Nectar Facebook: https://bit.ly/33Bzmpx Patristic Nectar Twitter: https://bit.ly/3igrH4f ———SUPPORT PATRISTIC NECTAR——— 1) Spread the Word - tell your family and friends about Patristic Nectar. Share Patristic Nectar website links to content you have enjoyed. A personal invitation is the number one way the Church grows. Tell a friend to "Come and see!" 2) Make a Donation -Patristic Nectar is a small non-profit ministry with a big vision for expanding access to Patristic Orthodox teaching throughout the world. Since our establishment in 2010, we have made steady progress but there is so much more we could do. With funding, we can work to make our ministry vision a reality. https://patristicnectar.org/donations 3) Pray For Us - remember us in your prayers, asking that the Lord strengthen, help, and direct us according to His divine will.

title: Easy Mucenici for 40 Martyrs of Sebaste | Ascetic Life of Motherhood
description: Easy Mucenici Ingredients: 1 Refrigerated Cinnamon rolls (large size) 1/2 cup walnuts (chopped) 1/2 cup honey (warmed) Directions: -Preheat oven to 350 F -Open cinnamon rolls. Unroll each cinnamon roll to a long roll, Cut each roll in half and create a ring by pinching the edges together. -Once you have the ring, twist it to form an “8” or infinity shape. -Place 2" apart on a prepared baking sheet. Bake for 12 mins. -Once out, let cool for 10 mins. -Heat the honey in a bowl for 1 min -Chop walnuts finely, and place in bowl -Once the buns have cooled, dip the top of the bun in honey, and then immediately dip in walnuts -Serve immediately and share with others! Can be stored in the fridge for up to a week. A simplified explanation of the Sunday gospel reading, making it relatable and engaging for kids. Thought-provoking questions to spark discussion and reflection. Inspiring messages to encourage your children's faith and love for Jesus. This video is perfect for children of all ages, whether they're new to the faith or have grown up in the Orthodox tradition. It's a wonderful way to introduce them to the beauty of the gospel and its teachings. 🔔 Don't forget to hit the "Subscribe" button and the notification bell so you never miss an episode of Father Jason's kid-friendly homilies! 🙌 Share the love! In this video, Father Jason will take your little ones on a spiritual journey, simplifying the Sunday gospel readings so that kids can better understand the Sunday Liturgy. 🙏 What to Expect: A warm and friendly introduction by Father Jason. A simplified explanation of the Sunday gospel reading, making it relatable and engaging for kids. Thought-provoking questions to spark discussion and reflection. title: Ascetic Life of Motherhood | Homemade Butter Recipe for Saint Brigid
description: Introducing a brand new series on PNP Kids! Get ready to embark on a delicious journey into the heart of Orthodox Christian traditions! Our newest content contributor Khouria Destinie Winn is bringing the warmth of family feasts, time-honored recipes, and rich traditions right to your screens! From mouthwatering dishes to festive celebrations, join us as we explore the flavors that unite generations! INGREDIENTS 3 CUPS HEAVY WHIPPING CREAM 1 QUART ICE-COLD WATER SALT TO TASTE (OPTIONAL) EQUIPMENT -STAND MIXER WITH WHISK ATTACHMENT OR HAND-HELD MIXER -SPATULA -TOWEL OR SPLASH GUARD -MESH STRAINER (OPTIONAL) 1. Add the whisk attachment to your stand mixer. Add heavy cream to the mixing bowl. Start the mixer on the slowest setting, gradually raising the speed to the fastest setting. Keep a dish towel on hand to cover the bowl if the cream splashes out. 2. The cream will go through three stages: soft peaks, then stiff peaks, and finally the butter solids will separate from the buttermilk. Once you see the butter solids separate, stop the stand mixer and pour out the buttermilk. (The buttermilk can be reserved for other uses.) 3. Transfer the butter to a fine mesh sieve set over a large bowl. Using a spatula, press the butter into the sieve to remove any excess buttermilk. (The less buttermilk that remains in the butter, the longer the butter may last.) 4. Clean the stand mixer bowl, then return the butter to it. Add 1/4 cup of ice-cold water to the bowl then whip the butter again for around 10 seconds to “wash” the butter and get rid of any excess buttermilk. Once the water becomes cloudy pour it out and repeat the process until the water remains clear. 5 Pour out any water remaining in the bowl. Replace the whisk accessory with the flat beater. Add any ingredients you want to flavor the butter to the bowl and beat until they are just combined. Finished butter can be formed into a log or put into a small bowl. Store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 weeks. Blessed Feast! Links | www.patristicnectar.org Donate | Text "PNP" to 53-555 to support our ministry! Follow | @PatristicNectarKids Kh. Destinie on Instagram @asceticlifeofmotherhood

title: "Repent!" with Fr. Jason (Matthew 4:12-17)
description: Orthodox Kids Homily: Understanding Sunday Gospel Readings with Father Jason (Matthew 4:12-17) Welcome to our special YouTube Kids edition of Father Jason's Sunday Gospel Homily! In this video, Father Jason will take your little ones on a spiritual journey, simplifying the Sunday gospel readings so that kids can better understand the Sunday Liturgy. 🙏 What to Expect: A warm and friendly introduction by Father Jason. A simplified explanation of the Sunday gospel reading, making it relatable and engaging for kids. Thought-provoking questions to spark discussion and reflection. Inspiring messages to encourage your children's faith and love for Jesus. This video is perfect for children of all ages, whether they're new to the faith or have grown up in the Orthodox tradition. It's a wonderful way to introduce them to the beauty of the gospel and its teachings. 🔔 Don't forget to hit the "Subscribe" button and the notification bell so you never miss an episode of Father Jason's kid-friendly homilies! 🙌 Share the love! title: “Baptism of Jesus” with Fr. Jason (John 1:29-34)
description: Orthodox Kids Homily: Understanding Sunday Gospel Readings with Father Jason (John 1:29-34) Welcome to our special YouTube Kids edition of Father Jason's Sunday Gospel Homily! In this video, Father Jason will take your little ones on a spiritual journey, simplifying the Sunday gospel readings so that kids can better understand the Sunday Liturgy. 🙏 What to Expect: A warm and friendly introduction by Father Jason. A simplified explanation of the Sunday gospel reading, making it relatable and engaging for kids. Thought-provoking questions to spark discussion and reflection. Inspiring messages to encourage your children's faith and love for Jesus. This video is perfect for children of all ages, whether they're new to the faith or have grown up in the Orthodox tradition. It's a wonderful way to introduce them to the beauty of the gospel and its teachings. 🔔 Don't forget to hit the "Subscribe" button and the notification bell so you never miss an episode of Father Jason's kid-friendly homilies! 🙌 Share the love! title: "The Way of The Lord" with Fr. Jason (Mark 1:1-8)
description: Orthodox Kids Homily: Understanding Sunday Gospel Readings with Father Jason (Mark 1:1-8) Welcome to our special YouTube Kids edition of Father Jason's Sunday Gospel Homily! In this video, Father Jason will take your little ones on a spiritual journey, simplifying the Sunday gospel readings so that kids can better understand the Sunday Liturgy. 🙏 What to Expect: A warm and friendly introduction by Father Jason. A simplified explanation of the Sunday gospel reading, making it relatable and engaging for kids. Thought-provoking questions to spark discussion and reflection. Inspiring messages to encourage your children's faith and love for Jesus. This video is perfect for children of all ages, whether they're new to the faith or have grown up in the Orthodox tradition. It's a wonderful way to introduce them to the beauty of the gospel and its teachings. 🔔 Don't forget to hit the "Subscribe" button and the notification bell so you never miss an episode of Father Jason's kid-friendly homilies! 🙌 Share the love! If you find this video meaningful, please share it with other families, and let's spread the joy of understanding the Word of God with our kids! 📖 For more spiritual content and resources, visit our website www.patristicnectar.org Please help us keep all of the kids' content for free. description: Orthodox Kids Homily: Understanding Sunday Gospel Readings with Father Jason (MATTHEW 1:1-25) Welcome to our special YouTube Kids edition of Father Jason's Sunday Gospel Homily! In this video, Father Jason will take your little ones on a spiritual journey, simplifying the Sunday gospel readings so that kids can better understand the Sunday Liturgy. 🙏 What to Expect: A warm and friendly introduction by Father Jason. A simplified explanation of the Sunday gospel reading, making it relatable and engaging for kids. Thought-provoking questions to spark discussion and reflection. Inspiring messages to encourage your children's faith and love for Jesus. This video is perfect for children of all ages, whether they're new to the faith or have grown up in the Orthodox tradition. It's a wonderful way to introduce them to the beauty of the gospel and its teachings. 🔔 Don't forget to hit the "Subscribe" button and the notification bell so you never miss an episode of Father Jason's kid-friendly homilies! 🙌 Share the love! The Scriptures are replete with teaching on the dark powers. Additionally, it is impossible to appreciate the magnitude of the saving deeds of our Savior, the Lord Jesus Christ, without understanding how He, and He alone, has conquered Satan and destroyed his works. Lastly, Christians are called to fight and win in the spiritual war, and for this reason, it is essential that believers understand their enemies and their tactics. description: July 28th, 2023 Father Josiah Trenham Download our Digital Catalogue here: https://www.patristicnectar.org/digitalcatalogue Origins: Creationism, Evolution, and an Orthodox Theology of Creation https://patristicnectar.org/bookstore_220620_1122222 Patristic Nectar Publications is pleased to present a new five-lecture series by His Grace, Irenei, Bishop of London and Western Europe for the Russian Orthodox Church Outside of Russia, entitled ORIGINS: Creationism, Evolution and an Orthodox Theology of Creation. Well-known patristics scholar and respected arch-pastor Bishop Irenei labors in this series to help believers approach the theology of creation from the presuppositions of the Church instead of through the prisms of evolution and creationism. description: April 19th, 2023 Father Josiah Trenham Origins: Creationism, Evolution, and an Orthodox Theology of Creation (FREE for the first week) https://patristicnectar.org/bookstore_220620_1122222 Patristic Nectar Publications is pleased to present a new five-lecture series by His Grace, Irenei, Bishop of London and Western Europe for the Russian Orthodox Church Outside of Russia, entitled ORIGINS: Creationism, Evolution and an Orthodox Theology of Creation. Well-known patristics scholar and respected arch-pastor Bishop Irenei labors in this series to help believers approach the theology of creation from the presuppositions of the Church instead of through the prisms of evolution and creationism. By an intensive examination of the foundational texts of Genesis, together with numerous sources from the Church Fathers, Bishop Irenei enables us to perceive the Church’s own theological priorities and emphases when addressing the subject of creation. title: The Humiliation of Hell
description: April 11th, 2023 Father Josiah Trenham Yielded to God: The Life and Teaching of Saint Seraphim of Sarov https://patristicnectar.org/bookstore_220620_1122221 The significance of the life of St. Seraphim upon contemporary Orthodox Christianity is so great that it is difficult to fully grasp. Though he was a humble Russian monk born in 1759 his influence has spread to become central and definitive in all the world-wide Orthodox Church. The life of the saints is a tapestry of a life wholly crucified to self and fully yielded to the will of God. His teaching on the purpose of Christian life as the acquisition of the Holy Spirit, and his great intimacy with the Most Pure Mother of God have captured the hearts of God-lovers and provided inspiration for spiritual acquisition for almost two centuries. title: Establishing Our Identity | Bishop Irenei
description: March 31, 2023 Father Josiah Trenham Bishop Irenei of London & Western Europe For more information on His Grace, Bishop Irenei, see here: https://www.patristicnectar.org/bishop_irenei If you are interested in other available titles, or if you would like more information on Patristic Nectar Publications, please visit our website at www.PatristicNectar.org ———LINKS——— Yielded to God: The Life and Teaching of Saint Seraphim of Sarov https://patristicnectar.org/bookstore_220620_1122221 The significance of the life of St. Seraphim upon contemporary Orthodox Christianity is so great that it is difficult to fully grasp. Though he was a humble Russian monk born in 1759 his influence has spread to become central and definitive in all the world-wide Orthodox Church. The life of the saints is a tapestry of a life wholly crucified to self and fully yielded to the will of God. His teaching on the purpose of Christian life as the acquisition of the Holy Spirit, and his great intimacy with the Most Pure Mother of God have captured the hearts of God-lovers and provided inspiration for spiritual acquisition for almost two centuries. title: Heaven is for Real
description: December 2nd, 2022 Father Josiah Trenham Instructions for downloading our web app: https://www.patristicnectar.org/app If you are interested in other available titles, or if you would like more information on Patristic Nectar Publications, please visit our website at www.PatristicNectar.org ———LINKS——— https://patristicnectar.org/ Heaven Our True Home https://patristicnectar.org/bookstore_220620_11 Patristic Nectar Publications is pleased to present a new 7 lecture series by Father Josiah Trenham entitled Heaven: Our True Home. One of the most shocking realities of the preaching and teaching of our Lord Jesus Christ to His early 1st century Judean audience was His fervent, expansive, and repetitive teaching on heaven. Heaven literally permeates the Sermon on the Mount and our Savior’s Parabolic instruction. The Holy Apostles received this single-eyed focus upon the next life from the Lord Christ and passed this teaching on to their disciples in the early Church. Sacred tradition has vivified and animated the discipleship of Christians in their race toward heaven ever since. In these lectures, Father Josiah opens the Scriptures and the writings of the Church Fathers on the subject of heaven in an effort to plant a deep impression of the future life of God’s children, and to stir up a great desire for obtaining it. Lecture titles are: Lecture #1 Heaven in the Holy Gospels Lecture #2 Heaven in the Acts of the Apostles and the Epistles Lecture #3 Heaven in the Apocalypse Lecture #4 Heaven in the Church Fathers: A Florilegium Lecture #5 Heaven: A Definitive End and a New Beginning Lecture #6 What is Heaven Actually Like: Common Questions Lecture #7 Heaven Mislaid: The Eclipse of Heaven in the Secular West and the Christian Response ———SOCIAL MEDIA——— Patristic Nectar Instagram: https://bit.ly/3kmupqE Patristic Nectar Facebook: https://bit.ly/33Bzmpx Patristic Nectar Twitter: https://bit.ly/3igrH4f ———SUPPORT PATRISTIC NECTAR——— 1) Spread the Word - tell your family and friends about Patristic Nectar. title: Overcoming Sadness in the Christian Life
description: November 29th, 2022 Father Josiah Trenham If you are interested in other available titles, or if you would like more information on Patristic Nectar Publications, please visit our website at www.PatristicNectar.org ———LINKS——— https://patristicnectar.org/ My Life in Christ: The Life & Teaching of Saint John of Kronstadt https://patristicnectar.org/bookstore_220620_11221 Patristic Nectar Publications is pleased to present a new 9-part lecture series entitled My Life in Christ: The Life and Teaching of St. John of Kronstadt. This series consists of two parts. The first consists of four thematic lectures given in 2022 by Fr. Josiah to the St. John Chrysostom Catechetical School in Riverside, Ca. The second part of this series is five talks given by His Grace, Bishop Basil of Wichita, at a men’s retreat in Kansas in 2008. St. John of Kronstadt, the Wonder-Worker, served God in Russia during the second half of the 19th century and fell asleep in Christ in 1908. His life, miracles, and teaching have been cherished by believers as God’s love gift to the Church and to the world on the cusp of the 20th century, the most violent century in the history of humanity. These lectures and discussions reveal the beauty of a life lived supremely in and for Jesus Christ the Lord. Lecture #1 - The Life of Saint John of Kronstadt Lecture #2 - On Prayer Lecture #3 - The Eucharist and Divine Liturgy Lecture #4 - On the Priesthood Lecture #5 - The Russia of St. John of Kronstadt Lecture #6 - Confession and Communion in St. John's Teaching Lecture #7 - Q&A (Part 1) Lecture #8 - St. John Counsels and Teachings on Prayer Lecture #9 - Q&A (Part 2) ———SOCIAL MEDIA——— Patristic Nectar Instagram: https://bit.ly/3kmupqE Patristic Nectar Facebook: https://bit.ly/33Bzmpx Patristic Nectar Twitter: https://bit.ly/3igrH4f ———SUPPORT PATRISTIC NECTAR——— 1) Spread the Word - tell your family and friends about Patristic Nectar. One of the most shocking realities of the preaching and teaching of our Lord Jesus Christ to His early 1st century Judean audience was His fervent, expansive, and repetitive teaching on heaven. Heaven literally permeates the Sermon on the Mount and our Savior’s Parabolic instruction. The Holy Apostles received this single-eyed focus upon the next life from the Lord Christ and passed this teaching on to their disciples in the early Church. Sacred tradition has vivified and animated the discipleship of Christians in their race toward heaven ever since.
